interconnectors.name: Eastern Green Link 1 (Torness to Hawthorn Pit)

ai_summary:
Scotland’s generation profile is currently demonstrating exceptional renewable strength, propelled by 4.4 GW of active wind output that anchors the nation’s role as a vital clean power exporter. Driven by this wind volume, Scottish carbon intensity has plunged to an admirable 32 gCO2/kWh. This underscores an operational window where renewable penetration successfully suppresses thermal generation, delivering near-complete regional decarbonization.

However, physical infrastructure bottlenecks continue to challenge overall system efficiency. Total wasted energy currently stands at 217.5 MWh, reflecting acute localized curtailment primarily driven by export limits across the B6 transmission boundary. While generation capability remains robust, the inability to transport surplus power south to demand centers incurs both economic costs through balancing mechanism actions and environmental loss via spilled clean energy.

To capture this latent value, strategic focus must pivot toward expanding flexible asset deployment, including utility-scale battery energy storage systems strategically sited north of key pinch points. In the long term, expediting planned high-voltage direct current subsea links remains critical to eliminating these 217.5 MWh friction points. Aligning high-capacity wind output with upgraded grid infrastructure will protect generator margins and maximize whole-system decarbonization without costly operational throttling.
